title: ISO 8601 Week Calendar
intro: An international week-date notation that identifies a date by its week-numbering year, week number and weekday.
summary: Weeks begin on Monday. Week 1 is the week that contains 4 January (and the year's first Thursday). An ISO year has 52 or 53 full weeks.
origin: ISO 8601 standardises the form of dates and week numbering for international coordination, scheduling and recordkeeping.
diagram_title: A YEAR MADE OF WHOLE WEEKS
structure: Every ISO week has seven days. The ISO week-numbering year can start in late December of the preceding Gregorian year.
diagram_caption: MONDAY TO SUNDAY / WEEK 1 TO 52 OR 53
pattern_note: The four blocks are a visual grouping, not official ISO quarters. Week numbers always continue in full Monday-to-Sunday weeks.
history: Businesses, researchers and international organisations use ISO week dates to distinguish Monday-to-Sunday workweeks without depending on month boundaries.
example: 1 January 2026 is Thursday of ISO week 2026-W01, written 2026-W01-4. Monday 29 December 2025 is already ISO 2026-W01-1.
limits: ISO week years and Gregorian calendar years can start and finish on different dates. Back-projected ISO dates are mathematical applications of a modern standard, not historical documentary usage.
